why: I compared the PASS and FAIL conditions of all seven verifier checks with the words of their expect lines. Checks 1–4 test exact stdout plus one newline, and check 1 also tests exit 0. The expect lines say "prints exactly … followed by a newline", so they require this. Check 5's escape reading ("backslash and t") matches the JSON text in the expect line. Check 6 uses `npm test`, as its expect line names it. It requires a test that runs bin/csv2json.js with --tsv on input containing tabs and checks the output. Its failure examples (only calling parse(), or asserting nothing) just restate what the words require. Check 7 requires only a mention of --tsv and an example invocation. The stricter items are all under "Advisory (does not affect PASS/FAIL)": the proof's "say that the flag means tab-separated", test:cli, the flag's position, parse.js staying unchanged, and the non-goals. No condition goes beyond what the words require.
